newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan President laments his nation's failings.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan President laments his nation's failings.

text.p: Pakistan President Farooq Leghari said on Monday the country had developed poorly in the past 50 years due to neglect of human development by successive governments despite good economic growth.

"I think Pakistan has done worse than any other South Asian country, our social indicators are amongst the worst in South Asia and perhaps worst in the world," Leghari told an international conference on human development in South Asia.
"We have merely paid lip-service, we have talked of increases in allocations to education, to health and other important areas for human resources development including population," he said.
"And yet all these promises, all the lip-service that we have paid is really gone (to) waste because we have never seriously tried to implement those ideas," Leghari said in a speech.
He described the situation as a collective failure of thinkers, economists and governments.
He said the poor state of literacy, health and education facilities in Pakistan was also due to budget cuts made by governments in social sectors, despite good economic growth.
"That is why I think Pakistan is lagging behind, and that is why most of the South Asian countries are lagging behind."

Leghari said the most important factor behind low development was lack of attention to human development. He said he hoped the new government of Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif, bureaucrats and leaders would keep this in mind while formulating policies.
World Bank representative in Pakistan Sadiq Ahmed said the scale of needs for human development investment in South Asia, particularly Pakistan, was greater than in any other region.
He said South Asia had an estimated 40 percent of the world's poor, one third of the world's children who were not in schools and one third of the world debts.
